whatItIs.text: Dried maize ground coarse to fine — polenta in Italy, mush and cornbread in the American South, ugali and sadza across Africa, masa harina when nixtamalized for tortillas.

historyNote.text: The same ground maize becomes a named staple almost everywhere it grows: polenta in Italy; nshima in Zambia, nsima in Malawi, ugali in the Great Lakes; cou-cou in Barbados, where it shares a national dish with flying fish.

howToChoose.text: Stone-ground retains the germ — more flavour, shorter life; steel-ground keeps about a year airtight. Fine or coarse depends on the dish, so read the recipe before the shelf.

storage.text: Keep airtight in a cool, dry cupboard; stone-ground prefers the fridge. The rulebook has the details.

foodSafetyRef.note: dry-goods storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Set cornmeal fries into crisp golden slices for breakfast; a dusting of it makes the crispiest crust on fried fish or roast potatoes.
